captions.detailed: A realistic model of a cross-slide milling vise. It features a wide, flat rectangular base plate in dark grey, a sliding cross-slide base that travels along a lower dovetail guide, and a main vise body on top. The vise body holds a fixed rear jaw and a movable front jaw that slides on an upper dovetail prismatic track, driven by a central metallic silver leadscrew. The entire mechanism is colored in matte dark grey except for the bright silver leadscrew.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a cross-slide milling vise using CadQuery. The model should include a flat rectangular base plate, a cross-slide base plate that slides linearly along a lower set of dovetail guides, a main vise body, a fixed rear jaw block, and a movable front jaw driven by a central silver cylindrical leadscrew on an upper set of dovetail prismatic tracks. Apply a dark grey matte finish to the body components and a metallic silver finish to the leadscrew.
captions.factory: The code constructs the cross-slide milling vise in multiple hierarchical parts. It starts by defining the flat rectangular bottom base plate. The cross-slide base is modeled with integrated lower dovetail guides. The main vise body is constructed with a fixed rear jaw block and an upper dovetail guide track. The movable front jaw is modeled as a matching block with a cutout for the dovetail slide. Finally, a central leadscrew is created using a cylinder primitive. Prismatic joints are defined to govern the perpendicular sliding motions of the cross-slide base and the movable front jaw.
